column3: The Hebrew has no repeated why in its final clause and names words of roaring; BSB adds a question about being far from saving him.
The Hebrew names silence rather than rest.

The Hebrew says they were not ashamed; BSB says not disappointed.
The Hebrew has man in the singular in the scorn phrase; BSB says men.
The Hebrew has lip and head in the singular; BSB has heads and describes sneering.
The Hebrew begins with a command to roll it upon the LORD; BSB says He trusts in the LORD.
The Hebrew has breasts in the plural; BSB has breast.

The Hebrew names the jaws; BSB says the roof of my mouth.
The Hebrew wording says like a lion at my hands and feet, without an explicit verb there; BSB says they have pierced them.
The Hebrew describes looking and seeing me without the added gloat in BSB.
The Hebrew has a lot in the singular; BSB has lots.

The Hebrew says from You is my praise and those fearing Him; BSB says praise for You and those fearing You.
The Hebrew has your heart in the singular; BSB has hearts.
The Hebrew says before You; BSB says before Him.

The Hebrew uses completed verbs for eating and worshiping and ends with a singular subject not preserving his life; BSB uses future and plural descriptions.
The Hebrew uses a passive verb of telling and does not explicitly add new to generation as BSB does.
